You are auditing part of a Kanban board for "Kodely" — a planned AI website/app builder whose moat is that sister company Nxeon owns the hosting infra (Proxmox VPS). You are doing a quality/completeness audit.

Read the full board dump at: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/board-dump.txt

Focus ONLY on these columns: "Tech & Architecture", "Admin Panel", "Trust, Legal & Compliance", "API Tokens", "Deploy on this vps". (Skim others for context.)

Key context: recommended stack mirrors Nxeon (Next.js/TS/Prisma/Postgres/Proxmox); the decisive/hard piece is the execution sandbox (self-hosted Firecracker microVMs on a separate Proxmox pool vs buy E2B/Modal); everything should be first-party to keep COGS ~$0 (only the Claude API is unavoidably paid); strong isolation is mandatory (a rival's agent once deleted a customer prod DB). Nxeon already has: auth, Stripe billing/dunning, coupon engine, self-hosted mail, first-party analytics patterns, RBAC + AuditLog.

Produce a CONCISE, structured report:
1. IMPROVE — specific existing cards that are weak/vague and how to sharpen them (reference titles).
2. ADD — genuinely missing cards. Think hard about: the sandbox/build-runner architecture, secrets management, per-tenant isolation, DB-per-project, autoscaling build workers, observability/tracing, disaster recovery/backups, cost-attribution telemetry, the Kodely↔Nxeon partner API contract, CI/CD for Kodely itself, data residency, abuse rate-limiting at infra level, key rotation, on-call/SRE.
3. ISSUES — duplicates, gaps between columns, risky assumptions.
4. TOP 5 — highest-leverage items (improve or add), ranked.

Be specific and terse. Return only the report as text. No preamble.

546	COLUMN: Tech & Architecture  (29 cards)
547	============================================================
548	
549	[URGENT/IDEA] Choose the preview runtime model (biggest architectural fork)
550	There are three proven approaches to the live-preview problem. StackBlitz **WebContainers** run a full Node.js runtime *in the browser tab* via WebAssembly (~1MB OS, zero per-user server cost) — this is what powers bolt.new ([blog.stackblitz.com](https://blog.stackblitz.com/posts/introducing-webcontainers/), [latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). **Cloud sandboxes** (E2B/Daytona/Modal) run the app on real VMs. **Lovable instead renders the iframe against a *real deployed instance*** of the app, which is why its preview reflects live database state ([vibe-eval.com](https://vibe-eval.com/guides/lovable-tech-stack/)). Kodely should pick deliberately: WebContainers give the cheapest instant preview but can't run Postgres/Prisma and fail in Safari; a server sandbox on Nxeon's own Proxmox VMs matches Kodely's likely Next.js+Prisma+Postgres output far better. Recommend a **server-side sandbox preview on Nxeon infra** as the primary path.
551	
552	[NORMAL/CHORE] Evaluate WebContainers licensing + Safari/SharedArrayBuffer limits
553	WebContainers boot Node in-browser in milliseconds and even re-run `npm install` on every load for a clean env, but they depend on `SharedArrayBuffer`, which requires COOP/COEP cross-origin-isolation headers and **does not work in Safari** ([sandpack.codesandbox.io/docs/advanced-usage/nodebox](https://sandpack.codesandbox.io/docs/advanced-usage/nodebox), [blog.stackblitz.com](https://blog.stackblitz.com/posts/introducing-webcontainers/)). WebContainers are also a commercial StackBlitz product with per-seat/enterprise licensing, not a free dependency. Kodely should treat WebContainers as an *optional fast-preview add-on* for pure-frontend projects, not the core, and confirm license cost before committing. Document the browser-support matrix so support doesn't get blindsided by Safari users seeing a blank preview.
554	
555	[LOW/IDEA] Consider Sandpack/Nodebox for lightweight frontend previews
556	CodeSandbox's **Sandpack** is an open-source (MIT) in-browser bundler with hot-module-reload and error overlays, and **Nodebox** runs Node in *any* browser (including Safari) because it avoids SharedArrayBuffer, with out-of-the-box support for Next.js, Vite and Astro ([codesandbox.io/blog/announcing-sandpack-2](https://codesandbox.io/blog/announcing-sandpack-2), [sandpack.codesandbox.io](https://sandpack.codesandbox.io/)). The tradeoff: Nodebox targets small projects/examples and can't reach full Node API compatibility. For Kodely's early free tier, Sandpack could power an instant, zero-infra-cost preview of generated React components before a project graduates to a real sandbox. Cheap way to make the first-render feel instant.
557	
558	[HIGH/FEATURE] Pick a cloud-sandbox provider: E2B vs Daytona vs Modal vs Fly
559	If not using Nxeon's own VMs, the market leaders differ sharply. **E2B** uses Firecracker microVMs (hardware-level isolation, ~150ms cold start, ephemeral) and reports 88% of Fortune 100 signed up; **Daytona** uses shared-kernel containers with faster ~90ms cold starts and *persistent* stateful workspaces better suited to long-running iterative agents; **Modal** and **Fly Machines** offer their own Firecracker-based compute ([northflank.com/blog/daytona-vs-e2b-ai-code-execution-sandboxes](https://northflank.com/blog/daytona-vs-e2b-ai-code-execution-sandboxes), [blog.logrocket.com](https://blog.logrocket.com/comparing-ai-agent-sandbox-platforms-e2b-modal-daytona-and-more/)). Note Daytona moved production closed-source in June 2026. Pricing is ~$0.05/vCPU-hr + ~$0.016/GiB-hr billed per second on both. Kodely should benchmark E2B (isolation) vs Daytona (persistence) against a self-hosted option before locking in.
560	
561	[HIGH/FEATURE] Self-host sandboxes on Nxeon Proxmox using Firecracker microVMs
562	E2B's isolation model is literally Firecracker microVMs — the same tech behind AWS Lambda — giving per-sandbox kernel isolation ([spheron.network/blog/ai-agent-code-execution-sandbox-e2b-daytona-firecracker](https://www.spheron.network/blog/ai-agent-code-execution-sandbox-e2b-daytona-firecracker/)). Nxeon already runs Proxmox VMs, so Kodely can run its own Firecracker (or lightweight VM/container) sandbox fleet on the same hardware, avoiding per-second sandbox vendor fees and keeping customer code on infra Nxeon controls. This directly reuses the existing Proxmox topology (the live .200 / dev .215 split noted in memory) — provision a *separate* sandbox host pool so builder workloads never touch the Soul Pilates prod box. Big cost + control win versus renting E2B/Daytona.
563	
564	[HIGH/FEATURE] Default generated stack: Vite + React + TS + Tailwind + shadcn/ui
565	This is the de-facto winning combo. Lovable generates a single-page React app scaffolded with **Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + React Router**, deliberately *not* Next.js App Router ([vibe-eval.com/guides/lovable-tech-stack](https://vibe-eval.com/guides/lovable-tech-stack/), [blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0](https://blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0/)). shadcn/ui matters because it's copy-in component source (not a locked dependency), so the AI can freely edit it and output stays consistent and good-looking. Kodely should ship this as the default template for pure web-app builds — it's fast to preview, easy for the model to reason about, and produces attractive UI out of the box.
566	
567	[HIGH/FEATURE] Offer a Next.js full-stack template (rocket.new / v0 style)
568	For apps that need server routes, SSR, and a real backend in one repo, rocket.new generates **production Next.js** apps and v0 generates full-stack Next.js with API routes and DB integration ([docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction), [blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0](https://blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0/)). This is exactly Nxeon's existing stack (Next.js + Prisma + Postgres), so Kodely can reuse Nxeon's build/deploy tooling and conventions with almost no new work for this template. Recommend two first-class templates — Vite SPA (fast/simple) and Next.js full-stack (Nxeon-native) — and let the planner pick based on the prompt.
569	
570	[HIGH/FEATURE] Backend choice: Supabase vs Convex vs Neon vs reuse Nxeon Postgres
571	rocket.new and Lovable both lean on **Supabase** (managed Postgres + auth + storage + realtime in one) as the default generated backend ([docs.rocket.new](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction)). Alternatives: **Convex** (TypeScript reactive backend, native embeddings/semantic search, great for realtime), **Neon** (serverless Postgres with branching + scale-to-zero, but no bundled auth/storage) ([bytebase.com/blog/convex-vs-supabase](https://www.bytebase.com/blog/convex-vs-supabase/), [encore.dev/articles/supabase-alternatives](https://encore.dev/articles/supabase-alternatives)). Kodely's edge: it can offer **Nxeon-hosted Postgres+Prisma as the default backend** (own infra, no Supabase bill, first-month-free hosting angle) while still supporting Supabase for users who want portability. Neon-style DB branching per preview is worth copying.
572	
573	[HIGH/FEATURE] Auth: bundle a batteries-included auth provider per template
574	Generated apps need working auth on the first build — rocket.new ships auth as part of every backend setup and lists multiple auth providers among its 25+ native integrations ([netnewsledger.com/2026/05/03](https://www.netnewsledger.com/2026/05/03/rocket-new-is-the-best-ai-app-builder-with-built-in-integrations/)). For the Supabase template use Supabase Auth; for the Nxeon Next.js template wire Auth.js/Lucia against the existing Postgres. 709	[URGENT/FEATURE] Build a flow-engineered agent loop: plan → generate → run → read errors → fix
710	Bolt.new's core insight is **flow engineering** (à la AlphaCodium): break app generation into smaller sequential steps rather than one monolithic generation, which works better across model capabilities ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). The loop is: produce a plan, write files, run the dev server/build, capture errors, feed them back, and iterate with fix/ignore options. Kodely should implement this explicit state-machine loop rather than a single prompt→dump — it's the difference between apps that boot and apps that don't. This is the single most important engine decision.
711	
712	[HIGH/FEATURE] Diff-based edits over full-file rewrites
713	Bolt applies changes as **diffs using speculative decoding**, changing only the parts that need updating — far fewer tokens and faster iterations than rewriting whole files, which matters at scale ([buildthisnow.com/blog/tools/extensions/claude-code-vs-bolt](https://www.buildthisnow.com/blog/tools/extensions/claude-code-vs-bolt), [latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Lovable by contrast plans first and rewrites larger sections, and is measurably slower (~60s vs ~30s per generation). Kodely should default to targeted diff/patch edits (search-replace blocks or unified diffs the model emits) and reserve full-file writes for new files or large refactors. Directly cuts token cost and latency.
714	
715	[HIGH/FEATURE] Model choice: Claude Sonnet as default, escalate to Opus for planning
716	Bolt.new and much of the category run on Anthropic's Claude (Bolt built an >$8M ARR business essentially as a 'Claude wrapper') because Claude leads at agentic coding ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt), [mastra.ai/articles/best-llm-for-coding](https://mastra.ai/articles/best-llm-for-coding)). Kodely already has Nxeon's Anthropic-based 'Build-with-AI' integration to reuse. Recommend **Claude Sonnet (4.5-class) as the workhorse** for edits/codegen and **Opus for the initial plan/architecture step**, with the model abstracted behind a router so a cheaper model can handle trivial edits. NOTE from memory: the Nxeon chat agent is still blocked on a valid/funded Anthropic key — Kodely inherits that dependency, so resolve billing first.
717	
718	[HIGH/FEATURE] Instrument the sandbox to feed real errors back to the agent
719	Bolt instruments WebContainers at the **process, runtime, and build levels** so the agent receives 'the state of the application and the errors from Node.js or the browser console' and can auto-fix ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). This closed error loop is why its output actually runs. Kodely must capture build output, dev-server logs, uncaught runtime exceptions, and browser console errors from the sandbox and pipe them structured into the agent's next turn. Without this, the model is fixing blind. Build the error-capture channel as part of the sandbox from the start.
720	
721	[HIGH/FEATURE] Context management for growing codebases — retrieve, don't dump
722	Bolt maximizes context ('the entire state of the application') for accuracy, but that only scales while projects are small ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Chroma's Context Rot study found *every* frontier model degrades as input grows — a 200K window can show serious accuracy loss by 50K tokens, and facts buried mid-context cost 30+ accuracy points ([cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely needs a retrieval layer: send the full tree/manifest but only the *relevant* file bodies (via embeddings + recent-edit heuristics), and keep the most important context at the start/end of the prompt. Plan retrieval before projects get big.
723	
724	[HIGH/CHORE] Prompt caching — the single biggest cost lever
725	Prompt caching gives a ~90% discount on cached input tokens and is the largest cost reducer for repeated system prompts; in Claude Code/Cline sessions, re-sending conversation history is ~50–60% of token spend and tool descriptions alone add 10–15K tokens per request ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/), [pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage](https://pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage/)). Kodely should structure prompts so the stable system prompt, tool definitions, and unchanging project context sit in cacheable prefixes with Anthropic cache breakpoints. This is low-effort, high-savings and should be wired in before launch, not retrofitted.
726	
727	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Context compaction / conversation summarization
728	Long build sessions bloat context; Claude's context-compaction can condense history server-side (one reported case collapsed 132K tokens to 2K) and 'isolating work across separate context windows' keeps tasks from contaminating each other ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/), [cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely should summarize resolved turns, trim stale tool output, and maintain a compact rolling project-state summary rather than replaying the whole chat each turn. Keeps long iterative sessions affordable and accurate.
729	
730	[HIGH/FEATURE] Tool-use design: give the agent fs, terminal, npm, and console tools
731	Bolt gives the model complete control of the filesystem, node server, package manager, terminal and browser console ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should expose a tight, well-described tool set — write_file, apply_diff, read_file, run_command, install_package, read_logs, restart_dev_server — each mapped to sandbox operations. Keep tool descriptions lean (they're billed on every call) and prefer a few composable tools over many niche ones. Good tool ergonomics are what let the model self-correct instead of guessing.

Vector DBs work but get expensive; a hybrid of efficient file storage + targeted embedding search often costs less ([pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage](https://pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage/)). Kodely should maintain a live project index (symbol map + embeddings, refreshed on edits) so the agent can grep/semantic-search to the exact files it needs. Reuse Nxeon's existing Postgres with pgvector rather than adding a new vector DB.

Kodely should define a strict output schema — plan block, then file-write and shell-command actions the runner parses deterministically — so parsing never depends on fragile prose. Invest real effort in the system prompt (stack conventions, when to diff vs rewrite, security rules); it's the cheapest quality lever and it's cacheable.

739	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Stream generation to the UI (files + reasoning live)
740	Modern builders stream file writes and reasoning as they happen so users see progress instead of a spinner; this is core to the bolt/Lovable UX ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should stream the model's tokens, surface each file being created/edited in real time, and show the plan up front. Streaming also lets users interrupt/redirect early, saving tokens on wrong directions. Reuse the streaming plumbing from Nxeon's existing Build-with-AI/chat agent.

Kodely must meter token/compute usage per user from day one, expose a credits balance, and price plans against real Anthropic + sandbox cost. 745	[HIGH/FEATURE] Execution-based evals: pass@k + a regression harness
746	Real codegen quality is measured by *running* the output, not reading it — generate code, run it in a sandbox, check against tests, with pass@k as the headline metric; system-level evals also cover retrieval, prompt design, tool use and guardrails ([promptfoo.dev/docs/guides/evaluate-coding-agents](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/guides/evaluate-coding-agents/), [futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026](https://futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026/)). Prevents silent quality drops when tweaking prompts or swapping models.

748	[URGENT/CHORE] Guardrails: prompt-injection, secrets, and code-injection scanners
749	Coding agents are attack surfaces — a Feb 2026 attack on the Cline IDE started with a malicious GitHub issue *title* containing injected instructions; defenses need input guardrails (screen prompts) and output guardrails (screen generated code) ([futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026](https://futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026/)). A SecretsScanner catches invented/leaked credentials and a CodeInjectionScanner flags eval/exec/shell-interpolation/template-injection in generated code. Because Kodely will read user repos, GitHub issues, and pasted content into the agent, it must sanitize untrusted input and scan every generated file before commit/deploy. ## Kodely Board Audit — Tech/Arch, Admin, Trust/Legal, API Tokens, Deploy-VPS

### 0. CRITICAL (read first)
The **"API Tokens" column is not a set of work cards — it is two pasted LIVE secrets**: a real Anthropic key (`sk-ant-api03-W5RJH24…`) and a Cloudflare token (`cfut_bbVmtUfqW5…`) with edit rights to kodely.site + kodely.me. A Kanban board is not a secret store. **Rotate both immediately, purge from the board/dump, and replace the column with a real design card.** This also contradicts the board's own "encrypted vault, never in prompts/logs" principle.

### 1. IMPROVE (existing cards that are weak/vague)
- **"Deploy on this vps" → "VPS"** — empty placeholder, zero content. Either delete or specify: which host, sandbox pool vs app host, and an explicit **"NOT the live .200 Soul Pilates box"** guard (per memory topology). Currently meaningless.
- **API Tokens column** (both cards) — replace raw keys with a proper "user-facing API token system" spec (scopes, hashing-at-rest, prefix + last-used, rotation, revoke) — the design already implied by the Admin "API tokens & keys oversight" card but never carded on the build side.
- **"Choose the preview runtime model" (URGENT/IDEA)** — still framed as an open fork, yet the "Recommended stack" card already decides (in-browser first, Firecracker pool later). Lock it to a DECISION card so eng stops treating it as unresolved.
- **"Public API + webhooks" (NORMAL)** — too thin. No auth model, versioning, signing, idempotency, rate limits, or webhook-retry semantics. Sharpen — especially since it underpins the Nxeon go-live bridge.
- **"Rate limiting, quotas & queue autoscaling" (HIGH)** — bundles three different concerns and conflates *app-level* limits with *infra-level abuse* controls. Split; call out infra-level egress/DDoS separately.
- **"Core data model / schema" (HIGH)** — lists entities but omits the tenancy-critical ones: per-project DB credentials, Secret/Vault, per-tenant isolation boundary. Reference the isolation model explicitly.
- **"System health & observability" (Admin, HIGH)** — broad and overlaps the Trust/Legal "status page + runbook" card. No distributed tracing, no SLO/error-budget, no on-call. Narrow it and cross-link.

### 2. ADD (genuinely missing cards)
1. **Disaster recovery + backups epic** — off-site backups (Nxeon memory flags this as a customer-readiness **BLOCKER**), per-project DB + filesystem snapshot restore, defined RTO/RPO, restore drills. *Biggest single gap — hosting other people's prod apps without this is negligent.*
2. **Kodely↔Nxeon partner API contract (formal spec)** — request signing, versioning, idempotency keys, auth, error semantics, webhook retry/DLQ. Only sketched inside the "Go-live flow" card; the whole moat rides on it.
3. **CI/CD + staging + build-isolation for Kodely itself** — Nxeon has documented build-in-prod outages ("never `npm run build` in the live tree"); Kodely needs its own promote pipeline, migration gating, and staging.
4. **Sandbox network egress / SSRF firewall** — egress allowlist, block access to Nxeon internal metadata/DB/control plane. This is the exact vector for the "rival agent deleted a customer prod DB" scenario; isolation card mentions "egress controls" in passing but it deserves a hard-gated card.
5. **DB-per-project lifecycle** — provisioning, isolated credentials, teardown, per-DB quota + backup. "DB branching" exists as a LOW/IDEA polish card but core per-tenant DB isolation is uncarded.
6. **Sandbox base-image supply chain + CVE patching** — golden image, dependency provenance, scheduled patch/rebuild.
7. **Service-key rotation runbook** — for Kodely's own Anthropic/Stripe/Nxeon-partner/Cloudflare keys (directly relevant given item 0). Rotation is name-dropped in one admin card, never designed.
8. **Distributed tracing / request correlation** across Kodely → queue → sandbox → Nxeon partner API.
9. **Anthropic capacity/dependency card** — org-level quota, spend caps, multi-key pool, funded-billing resolution as a launch blocker (memory: Nxeon chat agent still blocked on a funded key — Kodely inherits it).
10. **SLOs + on-call rotation + error budgets** — elevate beyond the single LOW "status page + runbook" card, given real customer sites are hosted.
11. **Data residency / region strategy** — only GDPR data-rights is carded; EU region pinning is separate and unaddressed.
12. **Load / chaos / capacity test of the build-worker pool** — validates the autoscaling claim before GA.

### 3. ISSUES (duplicates, cross-column gaps, risky assumptions)
